title: Leg artery ultrasound
also: arterial duplex scan of the legs
what: The doctor uses a probe to look at the arteries in your legs and check how blood flows through them. It is safe and uses no radiation.
why: For calf pain when walking, cold or pale feet, leg wounds that heal poorly, diabetes, or smoking.
tell_doctor: If your legs hurt when you walk, and after how many steps
If you have had surgery or stents on the blood vessels in your legs
Which blood pressure and blood medicines you take

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: No special preparation is needed. You can eat and drink as usual.

prepare.title: Smoking
prepare.text: Try not to smoke for at least 2 hours before the scan. Smoking narrows the blood vessels.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Wear something comfortable. You will need to take off your pants and socks. Best to skip tights.

bring: Past vascular ultrasound reports and surgery discharge papers
A towel or tissues, if you like
steps: You take off your pants and lie on your back
Sometimes your blood pressure is measured first on your arms and ankles
Gel is put on your skin
The doctor moves the probe from your groin down to your foot, then checks the other leg
Sometimes you are asked to lie on your belly so the vessels behind the knee can be checked
feel: Cool gel and light pressure from the probe
A pulsing sound from the machine. This is normal
A blood pressure cuff may squeeze your leg for a few seconds
after: The gel is wiped off with a tissue
You usually get the report right away
You can go back to your day right away
red_flags: If a leg suddenly turns cold, pale, very painful, or numb, do not wait for the scan. Call emergency services

faq.q: How is an artery ultrasound different from a vein ultrasound?
faq.a: Arteries carry blood to the leg, and veins carry it back. These are different scans. Your referral says which one you need.

faq.q: Do I need to prepare for a leg vessel ultrasound?
faq.a: No. Just do not smoke for a couple of hours before the scan.
